name: Lesotho
summary_text: Lesotho demands real caution. Same-sex conduct is legal (sodomy common-law crime struck down in 2012); the Rainbow Alliance of Lesotho documents failures to prevent violence, harassment and discrimination by state and non-state actors (2024 UPR submission); no LGR; small organised community inside South Africa's geographic envelope.

sources.claim_summary: Joint stakeholder UPR report (Oct 2024) by The Advocates for Human Rights, the Master of Healing Foundation and Rainbow Alliance of Lesotho on LGBTQ+ rights in Lesotho: documents discrimination, rape and assaults against LGBT people, barriers to health and education services, and community-level SOGIESC discrimination; same-sex conduct is not criminalised but no protections exist.

sources.title: Lesotho: ICJ makes a submission to the Universal Periodic Review | ICJ
sources.claim_summary: ICJ UPR submission (Nov 2024) on Lesotho: highlights LGBTIQ+ persons' rights to equality and non-discrimination among three key concerns (alongside inclusive education for children with disabilities and revocation of NGO lawyers' practising certificates).

SALC + People's Matrix Association + WLSA briefing (Oct 2020): 'Legal Gender Recognition in Lesotho' - analysis of law and policy against international best practice; Matrix is the only known LGBTI organisation in Lesotho; researched by Prof Alex Müller with community consultations.

US State Department 2016 Human Rights Report for Lesotho: documents the LDF mutiny arrests, torture of detainees, the killing of Lt-Gen Mahao, and the LGBT section noting no criminalisation but societal stigma.

SALC 'Transgender Rights in Lesotho' (2017): constitutional analysis - section 4(1) 'sex' and 'other status' should include gender identity per the UN Human Rights Committee; no law allows gender-marker changes; a trans person using a non-matching passport could be charged; the Labour Code's non-discrimination clause omits gender and sexual orientation.

Lesotho Labour Act 2024 (full text, ILO NATLEX): the new labour law - unfair discrimination, unfair labour practice, freedom of association, forced and child labour prohibitions - the current statutory framework for workplace rights.
